baseline: Transit error: Assumes Ninja House in Toshima is reached via the JR Yamanote line (10-15 min to Shinjuku), ignoring that Ochiai-minami-nagasaki / Toshima residential areas require the Toei Oedo or Seibu lines.

Severe geographic backtracking on Day 2: Sengokuhara -> Togendai -> Motohakone -> Gora (lunch & museum) -> Sengokuhara (Glass no Mori & supermarket) -> Gora (brewery dinner) -> Miyanoshita (bar) -> Sengokuhara (villa), causing massive unnecessary taxi expenses and transit exhaustion.

Food pacing error on Day 1: Schedules an all-you-can-eat and all-you-can-drink buffet at Tenseien (16:15–18:10) followed only two hours later by another multi-hour sit-down izakaya feast at MONTA (20:35–00:00).
Misleading onsen policy: Claims Hakone Yuryo has been 'tattoo-OK since 2025'; while private rental rooms allow anyone, Hakone Yuryo's public facilities still strictly prohibit exposed tattoos.

Flawed luggage logistics: Forwards luggage from Tokyo to Hakone and then forwards again from Hakone to Osaka on Monday morning, leaving the group stranded without their main suitcases in Osaka on Monday night (Yamato TA-Q-BIN inter-prefecture delivery takes next-day).

Tamura Ginkatsutei timing: Expects a walk-in group of 8 on a Sunday at 13:05 to clear the waitlist, be seated, and finish lunch by 14:25, which is unrealistic given peak weekend queues of 60–90+ minutes.
variant: Train numbering: Westbound Tokaido Shinkansen Hikari services stopping at Mishima are numbered in the 500s (e.g., Hikari 517), whereas 700-series numbers are generally Kodama runs.

Day 1 involves some backtracking by sending the group up to the Open-Air Museum and Gora Brewery in the afternoon, down to Yumoto for dinner and geisha games, and then back up to Sengokuhara late at night.

gemini.summary: Itinerary A is vastly superior in routing, pacing, and group ergonomics. It correctly identifies the classic logistics trick of forwarding main luggage straight from Tokyo to Osaka while touring Hakone with weekend bags. In contrast, Itinerary B commits severe routing errors (criss-crossing the Hakone mountains multiple times on Day 2), schedules back-to-back heavy drinking dinners on Day 1, and creates a luggage logistical headache in Osaka.

specificity.why: A gives exact train times (14:04→14:39, 18:05→18:43, Hikari 15:46→17:57), phone numbers, dishes and per-car taxi costs. B is often vague: 'a Hikari around 19:00', Round1 'prices at the counter', a buffet plan 'priced at booking', and unconfirmed Monday hours.

accuracy.why: Both get the dates right (19 Dec is the 3rd Saturday) and both handle the Sōunzan ropeway closure correctly. A slips on the Glass no Mori price (¥1,800 vs ¥1,700), an implausible 'Hikari 717' number, an optimistic 29-min taxi to Mishima and a contradictory sunset note. It does correctly reflect the Nov 2026 switch to refund-type tax-free. B likely has the geisha show time wrong (18:30 plus a 20:00 'second show'), overstates the Motohakone→shrine walk at 20 min, gives a 25-min pirate-ship crossing that conflicts with its own 45-min slot, and describes the outdated store-by-store tax-free process.

feasibility.why: A's routing is tight: day 1 Yumoto–Gora–Yumoto, then all of day 2's afternoon and evening clustered in Sengokuhara. B's day 2 zigzags by taxi from Motohakone to Gora, Sengokuhara, the villa, back to Gora, then Miyanoshita and the villa, with large uncosted taxi bills. B also carries villa drinks through a buffet and geisha show, and lands in Osaka at 21:25 for an unconfirmed Round1.

fit.why: Both suit 20-year-olds: geisha drinking games, brewpub and late bars. A adds a snack-bar karaoke night and a proper Tenma crawl plus a club. B's private mixed onsen and Tokinosumika beer hall are good group picks, but it starts drinking at 16:15 and overloads on taxis.

sourcing.why: Both lean on Google, Reddit and social posts, and both leave several items unsourced. A at least gives phone numbers and official tourism pages, though its Gora Brewery facts rest on TikTok and Xiaohongshu. B flags its uncertainties honestly but cites more 'Web search' and 'X posts'.

usefulness.why: A is executable as written, with booking to-dos matched to each slot. B needs more re-checking (geisha time, Round1 hours, bus times) and costs more in taxis for the same sights.

baseline: Furatto Geisha is given as an 18:30 show with a second at 20:00; the event appears to be a single 20:00–20:40 session.
Motohakone pier to Hakone Shrine is about 10 min on foot, not 20.
The pirate ship is said to take ~25 min to Motohakone, conflicting with the 45-min slot; Togendai→Motohakone is ~40 min.
Day 2 routing backtracks Motohakone→Gora→Sengokuhara→villa→Gora→Miyanoshita→villa entirely by taxi, with no taxi budget.
Tax-free is described as handled store by store; from Nov 2026 Japan uses a refund system with tax paid at the till and refunded at departure.
Hakone Yuryo's '2-hour' private slots and 'tattoo-OK since 2025' are dubious and unverified.
Round1 Sennichimae late hours are left unconfirmed for a 22:15–01:30 slot.
Romancecar is timed at 105 min (08:40–10:25), longer than the usual ~85–90 min.
variant: Glass no Mori price is contradictory: the header says ¥1,800 with Freepass discount, the How line says ¥1,700 after a ¥100 discount.
'Hikari 717' is implausible: 700-series numbers belong to Kodama services, and Hikari use 500s/600s.
A 29-min taxi from Gotemba Outlets to Mishima is optimistic; 40+ min is more realistic.
Contradictory dusk notes on day 3: 'dark before the Shinkansen leaves' vs a leftover 'Correction:' saying sunset is after departure.
A '30-min walk downhill' from a Sengokuhara villa to Togendai is unrealistic.
Open-Air Museum is listed at ¥2,000 'with Freepass discount', which is roughly the full adult price.
Day 1 morning timing is loose: check-out ends 09:50 but the first train isn't until 10:15.

judge.summary: A is tighter and more precise. Its routing clusters each evening sensibly, it gives exact connections and phone numbers, and it correctly reflects the Nov 2026 refund-type tax-free system, despite a few slips on prices, the train number and taxi timing. B has good ideas (private onsen, Tokinosumika beer hall) but likely mistimes the geisha show and wastes day 2 on costly back-and-forth taxis. It also leaves more critical details unconfirmed.
